metadata.case_name: DAVID JOHN SLATER v. COMMISSIONER OF POLICE

plaintiff.occupation_before: Chief Inspector posted to the Marine West Division, Marine Region of the Hong Kong Police
plaintiff.occupation_after: Director of Compliance and Loss Prevention, Advanced Merchant Payments Ltd. (from 3 June 2014)
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: Chief Inspector of the Marine Region

injuries.description: sprain injury to the low back
source: the plaintiff suffered from sprain injury to the low back and prolapsed intervertebral disc at the level of L5/S1, and that the sprain injury and prolapsed intervertebral disc were consistent with the circumstances of the accident as described by the plaintiff.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

injuries.description: prolapsed intervertebral disc at the level of L5/S1 (moderate degree L5/S1 disc extrusion, probably left S1 nerve root compression)
source: the plaintiff suffered from sprain injury to the low back and prolapsed intervertebral disc at the level of L5/S1, and that the sprain injury and prolapsed intervertebral disc were consistent with the circumstances of the accident as described by the plaintiff.
the findings in the MRI report were correct, namely, that there was a moderate degree L5/S1 disc extrusion, probably left S1 nerve root compression.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of nerve root of sacral spine

manifestations.description: pain in the low back region
constant pain throughout the waking hours (plaintiff's complaint)
ability to sit for about 20 minutes (sitting causes pain beyond that)
stand for about 20 to 30 minutes and walk for about 40 minutes (as estimated by plaintiff)
reduced straight leg raising to 35 degrees on the left side and 45 degrees on the right side
tenderness at the lumbosacral junction and both sacro-iliac joints

mild decreased (reduced) touch sensation of both feet (right sole and toes reduced by 20-30%; medial dorsum of right foot decreased by 10%; left sole reduced by 20%; left toes 20-30%; lateral dorsum of left foot 10%)

treatments_received: medical review and conservative management in public hospitals
treatments_future: attend an orthopaedic clinic about once every 3 to 4 months, and when there is exacerbation of pain, to ascertain deterioration of nerve root compression (advice of orthopaedic experts)
possible surgical intervention in future if disc herniation increases and causes nerve compression (not possible to predict)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Serious loss of amenities in not being able to play rugby and golf anymore.
